mainTopic: Items animals may not go out with on שבת, and the duty to protest wrongdoing (מחאה)
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about the rope a person holds when leading a camel on שבת. A ברייתא requiring the rope to stay a טפח off the ground refers to the stretch between the person and the animal. Then a new משנה lists items with which animals may not go out on שבת. The items belong to a donkey, roosters, rams, ewes, a calf and a cow. The משנה ends with the story of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's cow, which went out with a strap between its horns against the will of the חכמים. The גמרא explains each item in turn. It spends the most time on the puzzling word חנונות, rejecting two explanations as luxury care before settling on a sneezing remedy, and it defines גימון as a small training yoke. It then asks how a man with huge herds could have only 'his cow.' The answer is that the cow was his neighbor's, and it was called by his name because he did not protest. This leads to the teaching that anyone who can stop wrongdoing and stays silent is held responsible for it, whether at home, in his town, or in the whole world. The amud ends in the middle of רבי חנינא's explanation of a פסוק in ישעיה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to allow the rope to hang low
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier rule, which limited how much rope may hang below the person's hand, using a ברייתא that only requires the rope to be a טפח off the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: 'Provided that he raises it one טפח from the ground'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule just stated, which said the rope may not stick out more than a טפח below the hand. It brings a ברייתא that seems to say something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier rule measured from the hand: no more than a טפח of rope may dangle below it. The ברייתא measures from the ground: the rope only has to stay a טפח above the floor. That suggests a long loose end is fine, as long as it doesn't drag.

keyTerms.meaning: Provided that / only on condition that

steps.confusionAlert: Both rules use the measure of one טפח, but they measure from different places. The first measures down from the hand. The ברייתא measures up from the ground. Keep these apart.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: Provided that he raises (the rope)
phrases.notes: The word וְהָתַנְיָא signals a challenge from a ברייתא.

phrases.english: one handbreadth from the ground!
phrases.notes: This implies there is no limit on how much hangs below the hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיַּגְבִּיהַּ מִן הַקַּרְקַע טֶפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule earlier that the rope may not extend a טפח below the hand.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that no more than a טפח of rope may hang below the person's hand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא only requires the rope to stay a טפח above the ground. That implies any length may dangle below the hand, which contradicts the hand-based limit.

steps.title: The ברייתא refers to the rope between person and animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about the middle section of rope, between the person and the animal, not the loose end below the hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about the rope in between (the person and the animal).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge. The two rules are talking about two different parts of the same rope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loose end hanging below the hand may not exceed a טפח. The stretch between the person and the camel must not sag to the ground; it has to stay a טפח up. That way it is clear the rope is attached to the animal and the person is leading it, not carrying a separate rope. Both rules stand side by side.

keyTerms.meaning: When that (ברייתא) was taught. This phrase restricts a source to a specific case.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two separate rules for the rope. Below the hand, no more than a טפח may hang. Between the person and the animal, the rope must stay a טפח above the ground.

phrases.english: When that (ברייתא) was taught,
it was about the rope in between (the person and the animal).
phrases.notes: This is the stretch from the hand to the animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תַּנְיָא הַהִיא בְּחַבְלָא דְּבֵינֵי בֵּינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source refers to a different section of the rope.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא appeared to be about the loose end below the hand, which would allow it to hang down long.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about the middle section of rope. It must not sag to the ground, while the end below the hand stays limited to a טפח.

steps.title: Items a donkey may not go out with
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. It lists four items with which a donkey may not go out on שבת: an untied saddlecloth, a bell even if plugged, a neck frame, and a leg strap.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A donkey may not go out with a saddlecloth when it is not tied on, nor with a bell even if it is plugged, nor with a ladder around its neck, nor with a strap on its leg.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It lists things a donkey may not wear when going out into רשות הרבים on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that these items count as a load (משאוי) carried by the animal, or that they may fall off and the owner will carry them. An untied saddlecloth may slip off. A bell is forbidden even when plugged so it can't ring. The גמרא will later explain the reasons for each item.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; this marks the start of a new משנה
A saddlecloth or padded cloth placed on a donkey
Literally 'ladder'; a wooden frame on the neck that stops the animal from scratching a wound

steps.whyThisMatters: This continues the theme of the פרק: what counts as an animal's normal gear, which is permitted, versus a load, which is forbidden on שבת.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A donkey may not go out with the saddlecloth
when it is not tied to it,
phrases.notes: This implies that a saddlecloth which is tied on is allowed.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא בַּזּוּג אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא פָּקוּק,
phrases.english: nor with a bell, even if it is plugged,
nor with a ladder that is around its neck,
nor with a strap that is on its leg.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין חֲמוֹר יוֹצֵא בַּמַּרְדַּעַת בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵינָהּ קְשׁוּרָה לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It is unrelated to the rope discussion, but it continues the topic of the פרק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A donkey may not go out on שבת with an untied saddlecloth, a bell even if plugged, a neck frame, or a leg strap.

steps.title: Items roosters and rams may not go out with
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. Roosters may not go out with strings or straps on their feet, and rams may not go out with a small wagon under their tails.
steps.simpleTranslation: Roosters may not go out with strings, nor with a strap on their feet. Rams may not go out with a small wagon under their tails.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list, moving from donkeys to roosters and rams.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strings or straps were tied to roosters' feet as a sign of ownership. A small wagon was placed under a ram's heavy tail so it wouldn't drag and get hurt. Both are treated as items the animal may not go out with on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The fat tail of a sheep

phrases.english: And roosters may not go out with strings
nor with a strap on their feet,
and the rams may not go out with a small wagon
that is under their tail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roosters may not go out with strings or foot straps, and rams may not go out with a tail wagon.

steps.title: Items ewes, a calf and a cow may not go out with
steps.stepSummary: The list continues. Ewes may not go out חנונות, a calf may not go out with a גימון, and a cow may not go out with a hedgehog skin or a strap between its horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ewes may not go out חנונות, a calf may not go out with a גימון, and a cow may not go out with a hedgehog skin, nor with a strap between its horns.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list with ewes, a calf and a cow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Several of these words are unusual, and the גמרא will explain them later. A גימון is commonly understood as a small yoke used to train a calf. The hedgehog skin was tied on a cow, traditionally explained as protecting its udder from creatures that would suck its milk. All of these are treated as forbidden for the animal to go out with.

keyTerms.meaning: A term describing a certain way ewes were prepared; the גמרא will explain it
A small yoke placed on a calf

steps.confusionAlert: Don't try to work out חנונות from the words alone. The משנה gives no explanation, and the גמרא will define it.

phrases.english: And ewes may not go out חנונות,
phrases.notes: The term is explained later in the גמרא.

phrases.english: and a calf may not go out with a gimon (small yoke),
nor a cow with the skin of a hedgehog,
nor with a strap between its horns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes the list in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ewes may not go out חנונות, a calf may not go out with a גימון, and a cow may not go out with a hedgehog skin or a strap between its horns.

steps.title: The cow of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה reports that the cow of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה went out with a strap between its horns, against the view of the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The cow of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה would go out with a strap between its horns, against the will of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a story. It shows that one great sage acted differently from the ruling just given about a strap between a cow's horns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story reveals a disagreement. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה allowed the strap between the horns, while the חכמים forbade it. The phrase שלא ברצון חכמים tells us the accepted ruling follows the חכמים, so the last item in the list stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Against the will of the חכמים

steps.whatToRemember: This משנה lists items animals may not go out with on שבת. On the strap between a cow's horns, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה was lenient, but the חכמים disagreed, and their view is the accepted ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: A story recorded in a משנה can show a dissenting view in practice. The wording 'against the will of the חכמים' tells us the ruling does not follow that practice.

phrases.aramaic: פָּרָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: The cow of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
would go out with a strap between its horns
against the will of the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּרָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה הָיְתָה יוֹצְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a story with a dissenting practice about the last item in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה let his cow go out with a strap between its horns, but the חכמים disagreed and forbade it.

steps.title: Why the untied saddlecloth is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the untied saddlecloth rule. It answers that the reason is the one already given earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason? As we said before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה. It asks why a donkey cannot go out with an untied saddlecloth, and it answers that we already learned the reason earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new reason is given here. The גמרא points back to the earlier concern: an untied saddlecloth may fall off, and the owner may pick it up and carry it in רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason (for the untied saddlecloth)?
As we said (earlier).
phrases.notes: Refers back to the earlier worry that it may fall off and be carried.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's explanation of the משנה quoted in steps 3–6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The reason is the one already stated: the saddlecloth may fall off and the owner may carry it.

steps.title: Why a plugged bell is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A plugged bell makes no sound, yet it is still forbidden. The reason is that it looks like the owner is taking his donkey to market.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Nor with a bell even if it is plugged": because it looks like someone going to the market.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה, the plugged bell, and gives the reason it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think a plugged bell is fine because it makes no noise. The problem is how it looks. People decorated donkeys with bells for market day, so it seems as if the owner is heading out to do business on שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not noise, since the bell is plugged. The problem is the appearance of going to market.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא בַּזּוּג אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא פָּקוּק:
phrases.english: "Nor with a bell, even if it is plugged":
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: Because it looks
like someone who is going to the market.
phrases.notes: Donkeys were decorated with bells for market day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the משנה's donkey list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A plugged bell is forbidden because it looks like the owner is going to market.

steps.title: רב הונא identifies the neck frame
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that the "ladder" on the donkey's neck is a device attached at the jaw.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Nor with a ladder on its neck": רב הונא said: this is a jaw device.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's "ladder on its neck," and רב הונא explains what that object actually is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "ladder" is unclear, so רב הונא defines it as a frame-like device around the jaw. This sets up the next question about why anyone would put such a thing on a donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: Jaw device / something at the jaw

phrases.english: "Nor with a ladder that is on its neck":
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: רב הונא said: (it is) a jaw device.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the third item in the משנה's donkey list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The "ladder" is a device attached at the donkey's jaw.

steps.title: What is the jaw device for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what purpose this jaw device serves.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what purpose do they put it on the animal?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question. Now that we know what the device is, the גמרא asks why people use it, and the next step answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the purpose helps us understand the device. It tells us it is a functional tool, not a decoration.

phrases.english: For what (purpose) do they make it for it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רב הונא's definition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical purpose of the jaw device.

steps.title: The device keeps the donkey from scratching a wound
steps.stepSummary: The device is used when the donkey has a wound. It stops the donkey from turning its head and rubbing the wound again.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a case where it has a wound, so that it does not go back and scratch it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the jaw device protects a wound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The frame keeps the donkey's head from turning to rub or bite at an injury. So the device is a medical tool for the animal.

phrases.english: For a case where it has a wound,
so that it does not go back and rub at it.
phrases.notes: Keeps the animal from reopening the wound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is used on a wounded animal so it cannot turn and rub the wound.

steps.title: The leg strap protects the donkey's stride
steps.stepSummary: The strap on the donkey's leg is used to protect its stride, so its legs do not knock against each other as it walks.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Nor with a strap on its leg": which they put on it for its stride.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last donkey item in the משנה, the leg strap, and explains what it is for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some animals walk with legs that hit each other, which can cause injury. The strap protects the legs. Like the jaw device, it is a protective tool, not a normal part of the animal's gear.
steps.whatToRemember: For the donkey items: the untied saddlecloth may fall and be carried; the plugged bell looks like going to market; the neck frame (רב הונא: a jaw device) protects a wound; and the leg strap protects the animal's stride.

phrases.english: "Nor with a strap that is on its leg":
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: which they make for it for (protecting) its stride.
phrases.notes: Keeps its legs from knocking together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the fourth and last donkey item in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leg strap is put on the donkey to protect its stride.

steps.title: Why roosters wear strings
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says roosters may not go out with strings. The גמרא explains that the strings are an identifying sign so the roosters do not get mixed up with other people's roosters.
steps.simpleTranslation: And roosters may not go out with strings. The owners put strings on them as a sign, so they will not get mixed up with other roosters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה and explains what the strings are for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strings do nothing for the rooster's body or safety. They are only an ownership marker, so the rooster may not go out with them on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: So that it will not (a purpose clause)
They will get mixed up or exchanged

phrases.english: And roosters may not go out with strings:
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: for they put them on as a sign
so that they will not get mixed up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the item-by-item explanation of the משנה, moving from the donkey's strap to the rooster's strings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The strings on roosters are an ownership sign, and the roosters may not go out with them on שבת.

steps.title: Why roosters wear a strap
steps.stepSummary: The משנה also forbids a strap on roosters. The strap ties their legs so they do not jump around and break vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not with a strap. The owners put it on them so that vessels will not get broken.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next item in the משנה: the strap tied on a rooster's legs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the item serves a practical purpose. It limits how much the rooster can move so it does less damage. It still may not be worn out on שבת.

phrases.english: And not with a strap:
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: for they put it on them
so that vessels will not get broken.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּעָבְדִי לְהוּ כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא לִיתְבְּרוּ מָאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second rooster item from the same line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The strap on roosters is meant to stop them from breaking vessels.

steps.title: Why rams have a little wagon
steps.stepSummary: Rams may not go out with a small wagon under their tails. The wagon keeps their heavy fat tails from getting injured.
steps.simpleTranslation: And rams may not go out with a little wagon. It is put there so that their tails will not get injured.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next item in the משנה: a small wagon attached under a ram's tail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some rams had very heavy fatty tails that dragged on the ground and got hurt. The little wagon held the tail up off the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: They will be injured or bruised

phrases.english: And rams may not go out with a little wagon:
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: so that their tails will not get injured.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rooster items to the ram item in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wagon protects the ram's tail from injury.

steps.title: First explanation of חנונות: oiled wool after shearing
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר עולא explains that חנונות means ewes that, after shearing, have an oil-soaked piece of wool placed on their forehead so they do not catch cold.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ewes may not go out חנונות. רב אחא בר עולא sat before רב חסדא and said: from the time they shear the ewe, they soak a piece of wool in oil and put it on her forehead so she will not catch cold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches a hard word in the משנה, חנונות, and gives its first suggested meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A freshly shorn sheep has lost its warm wool. According to this view, an oiled swatch was put on its forehead to keep it warm, and an animal wearing that swatch is called חנונה.

keyTerms.meaning: A word in the משנה whose meaning is being worked out here
A swatch or piece of soft material

phrases.english: And ewes may not go out חנונות:
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Ulla sat
before Rav Chisda
and he sat and said:
From the time that they shear her
they soak a swatch in oil for her
and place it on her forehead
so that she will not catch cold.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב אַחָא בַּר עוּלָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא וְיָתֵיב וְקָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The earlier items were explained quickly. This item is unclear, so a longer discussion begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנונות are shorn ewes with an oiled swatch on the forehead to keep them from catching cold.

steps.title: רב חסדא: that is too much pampering for a sheep
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rejects the explanation. Treating a sheep this way would be like treating it as מר עוקבא, the ראש הגולה, which is not realistic.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: If so, you have made her into מר עוקבא!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא pushes back on the first explanation of חנונות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody puts oiled wool on every sheep just because it was shorn. That kind of care is fit for an important person like the ראש הגולה. So this cannot be what the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces an objection that follows from what was just said)

steps.confusionAlert: "You made her מר עוקבא" is not praise. It is a sharp rejection that means "you are describing royal treatment, not how people actually care for sheep."

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to him:
If so, you have made her into Mar Ukva!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects the explanation given in Step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole first explanation of חנונות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is unrealistic. Oiling a forehead swatch for every shorn sheep is luxury care fit for the ראש הגולה, not normal practice.

steps.title: Second explanation of חנונות: oiled wool during birth
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא בר שמואל offers a new meaning. When a ewe crouches to give birth, two oiled swatches are placed on it, one on the forehead and one on the womb, to keep it warm.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא בר שמואל sat before רב חסדא and said: when she crouches to give birth, they soak two swatches in oil and put one on her forehead and one on her womb so that she will be warmed.
steps.whatsHappening: The word אלא signals that the first explanation was dropped, and the גמרא brings a new one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This narrows the case to a short, risky moment: giving birth. Here special care might make more sense than for every shorn sheep. The new version also adds a second swatch, placed on the womb.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier idea and offers a new one)
So that she will be warmed

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא יָתֵיב רַב פָּפָּא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa bar Shmuel sat
before Rav Chisda
and he sat and said:
At the time when she crouches to give birth

phrases.aramaic: טוֹמְנִין לָהּ שְׁנֵי עֲזָקִין שֶׁל שֶׁמֶן,
phrases.english: they soak two swatches in oil for her,
and place one on her forehead
and one on the womb
so that she will be warmed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא יָתֵיב רַב פָּפָּא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא וְיָתֵיב וְקָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that was rejected in Step 17 with a new meaning of חנונות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנונות are ewes giving birth, with oiled swatches on the forehead and womb to keep them warm.

steps.title: רב נחמן: that is still too much pampering
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rejects the second explanation too. Treating a sheep this way would be like treating it as ילתא, his own aristocratic wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: If so, you have made her into ילתא!
steps.whatsHappening: The second explanation of חנונות is also rejected with the same kind of argument. The next step gives a new, more realistic explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even during birth, oiling two swatches for a sheep is care fit for a noblewoman like ילתא, who came from the family of the ראש הגולה. So the גמרא still needs a more realistic explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: רב נחמן's wife, from the family of the ראש הגולה, a symbol of noble pampering

steps.whatToRemember: Two explanations of חנונות have now been rejected for the same reason: each one describes luxury care that real farmers do not give their sheep.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:
If so, you have made her into Yalta!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the alternative explanation from Step 18, using the same kind of objection as Step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole second explanation of חנונות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is still unrealistic. This much care is fit for a noblewoman, not a sheep.

steps.title: A tree named יחנון whose chip makes ewes sneeze out worms
steps.stepSummary: After two explanations were rejected, רב הונא explains חנונות through a coastal tree called יחנון. A chip from it is put in the ewe's nose so she sneezes and the worms fall from her head.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב הונא said: There is a tree in the coastal cities called יחנון. People bring a chip of it and place it in the ewe's nose so that she sneezes and the worms on her head fall out.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the last two explanations of חנונות were rejected, רב הונא gives a third one: a practical medical treatment, not a fancy luxury.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier explanations failed because they described treating a sheep like royalty. רב הונא's explanation is a simple, realistic remedy. It also matches the word itself, because חנונות sounds like the tree's name, יחנון.

keyTerms.meaning: Coastal cities, towns by the sea
Name of a tree; the source of the word חנונות

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Huna said:
phrases.notes: אלא signals that the previous explanations are set aside.

phrases.english: There is a certain tree in the coastal cities
and its name is 'Yachnun',
phrases.notes: This name is the source of the word חנונות.

phrases.english: and they bring a wood chip
and place it in her nose
so that she will sneeze
and the worms of her head will fall out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third definition of חנונות after רב נחמן rejected the second one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנונות are ewes with a chip of the יחנון tree placed in their nose to make them sneeze out head-worms.

steps.title: Why only ewes and not rams too?
steps.stepSummary: If the treatment removes head-worms, rams should need it as well. So why does the משנה speak only of ewes?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, rams should also get this treatment!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא: rams have heads too, so why is the treatment described only for females?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word חנונות is feminine, so it refers to ewes. If the purpose were only to get rid of worms, the same practice should apply to rams. That would make the feminine wording strange.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; introduces a challenge based on what was just said

phrases.english: If so, rams too [should get this]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's explanation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rams have the same worm problem, so a treatment limited to ewes seems unexplained.

steps.title: Rams butt heads, so the worms fall off by themselves
steps.stepSummary: Rams knock heads with each other, which shakes the worms loose on its own. Only ewes need the sneezing treatment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since rams butt heads with each other, the worms fall out on their own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא by explaining why rams do not need the treatment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rams' natural behavior already solves the worm problem. Ewes do not butt heads, so only they need help from the wood chip. This explains why the משנה uses the feminine form.

phrases.english: Since rams butt heads with each other
[the worms] fall out on their own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction between males and females
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Rams should need the same worm treatment as ewes.
steps.terutzMaskana: Rams' head-butting knocks the worms off naturally, so only ewes need the chip.

steps.title: שמעון נזירא: the chip comes from a broom tree
steps.stepSummary: שמעון נזירא agrees about the sneezing chip but says it comes from a broom tree (רותם).
steps.simpleTranslation: שמעון נזירא said: It is a chip of a broom tree.
steps.whatsHappening: Another opinion names a different tree as the source of the chip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The practice is the same: a chip in the nose to cause sneezing. Only the tree changes. Since a broom tree is not called יחנון, this opinion loses the word connection to חנונות. That gap sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A chip of a broom tree (רותם)

phrases.english: Shimon the Nazirite said:
A chip of a broom tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel alternative to רב הונא's tree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sneezing chip comes from a broom tree.

steps.title: For the other opinions, why use the word חנונות?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's tree name explains the word חנונות. But the other sages' explanations have nothing to do with יחנון, so why does the משנה use that word?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works for רב הונא: that is why the משנה says 'חנונות.' But according to the other sages, what does 'חנונות' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a wording problem for every explanation except רב הונא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רב הונא, the word חנונות comes straight from the tree יחנון. The other explanations (oiled wool, swatches when giving birth, a broom-tree chip) give the word no source. So the גמרא asks how they account for the משנה's word choice.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rav Huna,
that is why it teaches 'chanunot',
but according to the other sages
what is 'chanunot'?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּרַב הוּנָא הַיְינוּ דְקָתָנֵי חֲנוּנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares all the explanations given so far on how well they fit the word.
steps.kashyaTarget: The non-רב הונא explanations of חנונות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only the יחנון explanation accounts for the משנה's specific word.

steps.title: חנונות means 'animals shown mercy'
steps.stepSummary: For the other sages, חנונות comes from חנינה (mercy), because these treatments show compassion for the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we do something for them that shows we have mercy on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word means 'shown mercy,' which fits all the other explanations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is read as coming from the root חנן, which means to be gracious or merciful. Every treatment mentioned, whether oiled wool, warm swatches, or a broom chip, is an act of care for the animal. So the word fits without needing a tree named יחנון.

phrases.english: Because we do something for them
that shows we have mercy on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question in step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the יחנון tree explains the word חנונות.
steps.terutzMaskana: חנונות means animals treated with mercy, which fits every explanation.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to read חנונות. רב הונא links it to the tree יחנון. Everyone else reads it as 'animals shown mercy' (from חנן).

steps.title: What is a calf with a גימון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה, that a calf may not go out with a גימון, and asks what a גימון is.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And a calf may not go out with a גימון.' What is a calf with a גימון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and asks for the meaning of an unclear word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic. The word גימון is unfamiliar, so the גמרא first defines it. The answer will come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: An unclear word, defined in the next steps

phrases.english: And a calf may not go out with a gimon.
phrases.notes: Quotation from the משנה.

phrases.english: What is 'a calf with a gimon'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the חנונות discussion and starts the next clause of the משנה.

steps.title: רב הונא: a small training yoke
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that a גימון is a small yoke put on a young calf to train it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: A small yoke.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question: a גימון is a small yoke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The calf wears a mini yoke so it gets used to bearing one when it grows up. It is not needed to guard or protect the calf, so it counts as a load (משוי) and is not allowed on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A small yoke (literally 'son of a yoke')

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: A small yoke.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גימון is a small training yoke.

steps.title: A פסוק shows that גימון means bending
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר proves from ישעיהו (58:5), 'to bow his head like an אגמון,' that the word means bending, which fits a yoke that bends the calf's neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: How do we know that this word גימון means bending? Because it is written: 'Is it to bow his head like a bulrush (אגמון)?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר brings a פסוק as a source for the meaning of גימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אגמון, a bulrush that bends over, sounds like גימון and is used for bowing the head. So גימון means something that bends, which supports רב הונא's 'small yoke' that bends the calf's neck down.

keyTerms.meaning: A bulrush, a reed that bends

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
From where is it inferred that this 'gimon'
is a term of bending?
As it is written:
'Is it to bow his head like a bulrush?'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 58:5

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי גִּימוֹן לִישָּׁנָא דְּמֵיכַף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the definition in step 27 with a source from תנ״ך.
steps.raayaObject: That גימון means something that bends (a yoke).

steps.title: A cow with a hedgehog skin, to stop creatures from sucking its milk
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a cow may not go out with a hedgehog skin. The גמרא explains that the skin is put on so small creatures will not suck milk from her udder.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And not a cow with the skin of a hedgehog': they do this to her so that creeping creatures will not suck milk from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה and explains why people put a hedgehog skin on a cow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prickly skin over the udder protects the milk, not the cow's body. Since it is not a normal guarding item for the animal, it counts as a load on שבת.

phrases.english: And not a cow with the skin of a hedgehog:
phrases.notes: Quotation from the משנה.

phrases.english: that they do it to her
so that creeping creatures will not suck from her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The hedgehog skin protects the cow's milk from creatures, so it is not allowed on שבת.

steps.title: The strap between the horns according to רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה, that a cow may not go out with a strap between its horns. It then explains how this rule works according to each side of the earlier argument between רב and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says a cow may not go out with a strap between its horns. According to רב, this is forbidden whether the strap is for decoration or for holding the animal. According to שמואל, it is forbidden only if it is for decoration. If it is for holding the animal, it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, a strap between a cow's horns. It shows how the two opinions we already learned, רב's and שמואל's, would each read this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the daf, רב and שמואל argued about this very strap. רב forbids it in every case. שמואל splits it: a strap worn as decoration counts as a 'load' (משאוי) and is forbidden, but a strap that guards the animal is like a normal leash (שמירה) and is permitted. So the short words of the משנה mean something different depending on whose view you follow.

keyTerms.meaning: To guard or hold the animal (like a leash)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב and שמואל are arguing for the first time here. The גמרא is only applying their earlier argument to this clause of the משנה.

phrases.english: And not with a strap that is between its horns.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: If according to Rav, who said:
Whether for decoration or to guard, it is forbidden.
If according to Shmuel, who said:
For decoration, forbidden; to guard, permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the משנה's list after the hedgehog skin
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, the strap between the horns is always forbidden. According to שמואל, it is forbidden only when worn for decoration and permitted when it guards the animal.

steps.title: Did רבי אלעזר בן עזריה really have only one cow?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה mentions 'the cow' of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. The גמרא challenges this, since we know he was very rich and tithed 12,000 calves from his herds every year.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה speaks of 'the cow of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.' Did he have only one cow? But רב said (and some say רב יהודה said in the name of רב) that every year רבי אלעזר בן עזריה gave 12,000 calves from his herds as tithe!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a sharp question about the wording of the משנה. How can it say 'his cow,' as if he had only one, when he owned enormous herds?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tithing 12,000 calves means about 120,000 calves were born in his herds each year, because one out of every ten is given as מעשר בהמה. With so many animals, calling one of them 'the cow of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה' makes no sense. The challenge targets the wording of the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: פָּרָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה:
phrases.english: The cow of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya:
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: Did he have only one cow?
But didn't Rav say,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לָהּ אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
Twelve thousand calves

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה מְעַשַּׂר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה מֵעֶדְרֵיהּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya would tithe from his herds
each and every year.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲדָא פָּרָה הַוְיָא לֵיהּ? וְהָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the rule about the strap to the story in the משנה about רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's cow
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's phrase 'the cow of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A man who tithed 12,000 calves a year had huge herds, so it is strange to speak of 'his cow' as if he had only one.

steps.title: It was his neighbor's cow, named after him because he did not protest
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא answers that the cow belonged to his neighbor, a woman. Because he did not protest her conduct, the cow was called by his name.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: the cow was not his. It belonged to his neighbor. Since he did not protest against her, it was called by his name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא. The cow was not his at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His neighbor let her cow go out on שבת with the strap against the wishes of the חכמים. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה could have stopped her and did not. So the wrongdoing is pinned on him, and the cow is 'called by his name.' This is not praise. It is a mark of blame.

keyTerms.meaning: It was called by his name

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer introduces the idea of מחאה, the duty to protest wrongdoing. The next teaching builds on it directly.

phrases.english: It was taught:
It was not his;
rather, it was his neighbor's;
and because he did not protest against her,
it was called by his name.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: לֹא שֶׁלּוֹ הָיְתָה אֶלָּא שֶׁל שְׁכֶינְתּוֹ הָיְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 31
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the cow belonged to someone else
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה means a cow that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה himself owned
steps.terutzMaskana: It was his neighbor's cow, called by his name because he failed to protest

steps.title: Whoever can protest and does not is held responsible
steps.stepSummary: Several אמוראים teach that a person who could have protested wrongdoing and did not is held responsible for it. The responsibility grows with his reach: his household, his town, or the whole world. The גמרא also notes a correction to the names in this list.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב, רבי חנינא, רבי יוחנן, and רב חביבא taught (throughout סדר מועד, wherever this pair appears, take out רבי יוחנן and put in רבי יונתן): Anyone who could protest against the people of his household and did not is held responsible for the people of his household. If he could protest against the people of his town, he is held responsible for the people of his town. If he could protest against the whole world, he is held responsible for the whole world.
steps.whatsHappening: Following the story of the neighbor's cow, the גמרא brings a general teaching about the duty to protest. Along the way it pauses briefly to fix one of the names in the list of teachers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name correction says that throughout סדר מועד, in this pairing, the name should read רבי יונתן and not רבי יוחנן. The teaching itself says your responsibility matches your influence. If you could have stopped wrongdoing and stayed silent, it is counted against you: at home, in your town, or in the whole world. This explains why the cow was 'called by his name.'

keyTerms.meaning: To protest, to stop someone from wrongdoing
Is caught, held responsible and punished

steps.whatToRemember: Silence is not neutral. If you have the power to stop wrongdoing and do not, you share the blame, and the circle of blame matches the circle of your influence. That is why the neighbor's cow carried רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's name.
steps.confusionAlert: The line about swapping רבי יוחנן for רבי יונתן is only a correction to the names. It is not part of the teaching about protesting.

phrases.aramaic: רַב וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַב חֲבִיבָא מַתְנוּ:
phrases.english: Rav, Rabbi Ḥanina, Rabbi Yoḥanan, and Rav Ḥaviva taught:
Throughout the order of Moed,
phrases.notes: This is a side remark to help get the names right.

phrases.english: wherever this pair appears,

phrases.aramaic: חַלּוֹפֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וּמְעַיֵּיל רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן.
phrases.english: take out Rabbi Yoḥanan and put in Rabbi Yonatan.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִי שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לִמְחוֹת לְאַנְשֵׁי בֵיתוֹ
phrases.english: Anyone who is able to protest against the people of his household
and did not protest
is held responsible for the people of his household.
[If he could protest] against the people of his town,
he is held responsible for the people of his town.
[If he could protest] against the whole world,
he is held responsible for the whole world.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מִי שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לִמְחוֹת לְאַנְשֵׁי בֵיתוֹ וְלֹא מִיחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the idea in step 32 (blamed for not protesting) into a general principle
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who can protest wrongdoing and does not is held responsible for it, in proportion to his sphere of influence: household, town, or the whole world.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic Talmudic source for the duty of מחאה and for shared responsibility for other people's wrongdoing.

steps.title: The Exilarch's household is held responsible for the whole world
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the household of the ריש גלותא is held responsible for the sins of the whole world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: And the members of the household of the ריש גלותא are held responsible for the whole world.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא applies the rule from the last step to a real case. Because the ריש גלותא's household had power over all of Jewish society, they are held responsible for everyone's sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 33 taught that responsibility grows with how far a person's influence reaches. The ריש גלותא's authority reached the whole Jewish world. So his household falls into the widest group, the people held responsible for the entire world.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, the official leader of the Jews in Babylonia
Are seized, held responsible, or punished
The whole world (here, all of the Jewish people)

steps.whyThisMatters: This turns the general rule into a real-life lesson: the more power a leader has, the more he is held responsible for wrongdoing he does not stop.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
And these members of the Exilarch's household
phrases.notes: The ריש גלותא had authority over Jews everywhere.

phrases.english: are held responsible for the whole world.
phrases.notes: Because they could have protested anywhere, they are punished for sins everywhere.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: וְהָנֵי דְּבֵי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from Step 33 about responsibility for the whole world to the household of the ריש גלותא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The household of the ריש גלותא is held responsible for the sins of the whole Jewish world, because they had the power to protest everywhere.

steps.title: A פסוק about ה׳ judging the elders and the princes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings support from רבי חנינא, who explains the פסוק saying ה׳ will judge the elders together with the princes. He begins to ask why the elders are judged if only the princes sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רבי חנינא said: What is the meaning of the פסוק, 'ה׳ will enter into judgment with the elders of His people and its princes'? If the princes sinned...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source from the תנ״ך to support the idea that people are punished for wrongdoing they did not stop. This step is a setup: רבי חנינא starts a question about the פסוק, and the question and answer continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ה׳ will judge both the elders and the princes. The robbery in the פסוק was done by the princes. רבי חנינא is about to ask why the elders are punished at all. His answer, coming next, will be that they did not protest against the princes.

keyTerms.meaning: Like this, as shown by this (introduces a supporting source)
What is the meaning of what is written?
The elders of His people, the wise leaders

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence 'אם שרים חטאו' is not finished here. It is the first half of a question: 'If the princes sinned, what did the elders do wrong?' The question and its answer come in the next part of the text.

phrases.english: As that which Rabbi Ḥanina said:
phrases.notes: Brings a supporting source for רב פפא's idea.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of that which is written:
"The Lord will enter into judgment
phrases.notes: ישעיה ג:יד

phrases.english: with the elders of His people and its princes"?
phrases.notes: Both groups are judged together.

phrases.english: If the princes sinned,
phrases.notes: The start of a question. It continues: why are the elders judged too?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מַאי דִכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a supporting פסוק for the rule that leaders are held responsible for wrongdoing they fail to stop.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that someone who could protest and does not is punished for others' sins.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חנינא's explanation of ישעיה ג:יד, where ה׳ judges the elders together with the princes. The explanation is completed on the next amud.
